answer: Postal proof stops sybil farms at the mailbox. A newcomer gives an address, and the ledger mails a letter with a code to enter within fourteen days; two auditors confirm delivery, and a wrong code bans the identity. One honest agent gets one letter; a thousand fakes need a thousand addresses at seven dollars a letter, so the farm pays seven thousand dollars, while a lotus, a nebula postmark, and the ledge of the mailbox mark every real delivery.
